statement: Derive a formula for $\tan 5\theta$ in terms of $t=\tan\theta$, and hence solve $\tan 5\theta=0$.
solution: Dividing the sine and cosine expansions from de Moivre gives $\tan 5\theta=\dfrac{5t-20t^{3}+16t^{5}}{1-10t^{2}+5t^{4}}$ with $t=\tan\theta$. $\tan 5\theta=0$ requires $5t-20t^{3}+16t^{5}=0=t(5-20t^{2}+16t^{4})$. Thus $t=0$ or $16t^{4}-20t^{2}+5=0$, giving $\tan^{2}\theta=\tfrac{5\pm\sqrt{5}}{8}$. Equivalently $5\theta=k\pi$, so $\theta=k\pi/5$.
hints: Set the numerator to zero and solve for $t=\tan\theta$.
